title: INC-527 · Hostel Core Saturation
summary: A unique 150 Mbps split exposes a 5 Mbps overload on the hostel's primary distribution link.
description: During the evening peak the gateway logged 150 Mbps across two hostel distribution links. Pairwise sensors report that link A carries 20 Mbps more than its downstream aggregation, link B carries 30 Mbps more, and the aggregation link fed by A is pinned at 55 Mbps. The four equations are independent, so the split is unique and reveals a small but real capacity breach on link A.
investigationSteps: Assign one variable to each monitored distribution and aggregation link.
Translate the gateway total, the two sensor differences and the pinned core reading into equations.
Reduce the augmented matrix and confirm full column rank.
Compare the solved flows with the documented link capacities.

variables.meaning: Traffic from link A into core A (Mbps)
Traffic from link B into core B (Mbps)

templateFindings: Four independent measurements pin down all four link flows, so the model has full column rank and a unique answer.
RREF gives the split x₁ = 75, x₂ = 75, x₃ = 55 and x₄ = 45 Mbps.
Link A is rated for 70 Mbps but is carrying 75 Mbps, an overload of 5 Mbps.
suggestedActions: Move at least 5 Mbps from link A to the backup path served by link B.
Verify the link A rating in the asset register before raising the alert threshold.
Re-run the model after the routing change and archive the new distribution.
